newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids down as MGE slips.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids down as MGE slips.

text.p: Dark northern spring and white wheat cash bids were mostly lower on Wednesday, in line with a drop in MGE wheat futures, with light farmer selling noted, several cash grain dealers said.
"We haven't seen many trucks in here, partly because (farmers) are busy with harvest and partly because of the prices," a North Dakota dealer said.
MGE spring wheat futures ended down 7-3/4 cents per bushel in the December contract on fund long liquidation.
In Montana, harvest was nearly complete but one dealer said producers were reluctant to sell new crop wheat.
"They saw $5.00 (per bushel) this year and they don't want to settle for anything less," he said. Bids in Montana ranged from $4.35 to $4.50 per bushel on Wednesday.
"I think $5.00 would buy a lot of wheat," another Montana dealer said.
